item.title: Navatu Secondary flying North’s flag in Super Deans semi-finals
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/08/2026 The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has defied the odds and will fly the flag for the Northern Division at this week’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 12/08/2026

The Navatu Secondary School Under-19 rugby team has defied the odds and will fly the flag for the Northern Division at this week’s Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans semi-finals.

Navatu Secondary is located in Cakaudrove Province on Vanua Levu and is the only team from the North to have reached the semifinals.

The team had a grand celebration as it departed Vanua Levu for Suva, bringing with it the blessings of the vanua and the people.

Navatu Secondary School has been consistent in the Under-19 division, defeating Queen Victoria School 19-12 in the national playoffs before overcoming Suva Grammar School 19-15 in the quarter-finals.

This Saturday, Navatu Secondary will face Ratu Kadavulevu School at 1.50pm at Buckhurst Park.

In the Under-18 semi-finals, Suva Grammar School will meet Ra High School at 3pm at Churchill Park in Lautoka, while Lelean Memorial School will face Nasinu Secondary School at 3.40pm at HFC Bank Stadium.

item.title: Delta Tigers roar back with 4-2 win to keep OFC semi-final hopes alive
item.description: Rewa FC have bounced back strongly with a 4-2 victory over Solomons's Tupapa Maraerenga in their OFC Men’s Champions League campaign. Ramzan Khan opened the scoring for Rewa in the 39th minute, giving the Delta Tigers a 1-nil lead heading into halftime.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC have bounced back strongly with a 4-2 victory over Solomons's Tupapa Maraerenga in their OFC Men’s Champions League campaign.

Ramzan Khan opened the scoring for Rewa in the 39th minute, giving the Delta Tigers a 1-nil lead heading into halftime.

Rewa came out firing in the second half, with Joseph Athale finding the back of the net in the 47th minute to extend their lead.

Setareki Hughes added Rewa’s third goal in the 66th minute, with Josaia Sela scoring in the 85th minute to help secure the victory.

The win gives Rewa and their fans renewed hope as they look ahead to their next match.

They need to win their next match to qualify for the semi final.

Rewa will now turn their attention to their next match against Solomon Islands' Lae City this Saturday at 3pm at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

item.title: OFC Men's Champions League: Nabenu calls for greater hunger as Rewa target crucial win
item.description: Rewa suffered a disappointing 4–1 defeat in their opening match against Vanuatu's Galaxy FC, despite creating several scoring opportunities. With their hopes of progressing further into the tournament now under pressure, Nabenu says the team understands the importance of securing all three points.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa suffered a disappointing 4–1 defeat in their opening match against Vanuatu's Galaxy FC, despite creating several scoring opportunities.

With their hopes of progressing further into the tournament now under pressure, Nabenu says the team understands the importance of securing all three points.

Nabenu believes Rewa do not need a major overhaul, but says the team must be more clinical when opportunities come their way.

He also urged supporters to turn out and back Rewa in their crucial encounter.

Rewa FC will take on Tupapa Maraerenga FC at 4pm at 4R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba.

The Delta Tigers will play their final group match against Lae City FC of Papua New Guinea on Saturday at 3pm at the same venue.

They need positive results in both matches to keep their hopes of reaching the semi-finals alive.

item.title: Ra High ready to roar again - Wakili the man to watch
item.description: Ra High School will head into this week’s National Vodafone Super Deans Competition clash with plenty of confidence after producing one of the biggest statements of last week’s quarter-finals. The Ra boys stunned former Super Deans champions Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), sending a clear message that they are not in the competition just to make up the numbers.
item.content:encoded:
Ra High School will head into this week’s National Vodafone Super Deans Competition clash with plenty of confidence after producing one of the biggest statements of last week’s quarter-finals.

The Ra boys stunned former Super Deans champions Ratu Kadavulevu School (RKS), sending a clear message that they are not in the competition just to make up the numbers.

One player who caught the eye in that impressive victory was inside centre Jack Wakili, who crossed the try line twice against RKS.

Wakili, who hails from Maniava Takaimalo in Ra, has impressive speed and attacking instincts, along with a sneaky sidestep.

He will form a formidable midfield combination with Joseva Boto from Bua at outside centre, giving Ra High a dangerous one-two punch in the backs.

The pair will be expected to test the Lions’ defensive line with their strength, speed and ability to create opportunities in broken play.

Ra High School will play Suva Grammar School at Churchill Park in Lautoka.

The time for the match has not been confirmed yet.

item.title: Flying Fijian Wainiqolo completes challenging Naboro Obstacle Course
item.description: France-based Flying Fijian and Olympian Jiuta Wainiqolo completes the challenging Naboro Obstacle Course at the Naboro Corrections Facility. The obstacle course at the Fiji Corrections training facility is a demanding test designed to challenge mental toughness, resilience, determination and physical fitness.
item.content:encoded:
France-based Flying Fijian and Olympian Jiuta Wainiqolo completes the challenging Naboro Obstacle Course at the Naboro Corrections Facility.

The obstacle course at the Fiji Corrections training facility is a demanding test designed to challenge mental toughness, resilience, determination and physical fitness.

Wainiqolo is currently in the country and never lets his guard down when it comes to maintaining his fitness and discipline.

During his visit, Wainiqolo also met fellow Olympian Josua Vakurunabili, who currently serves with the Fiji Corrections Service Emergency Control Unit.

Known in France as the “Fijian Ferrari”, Wainiqolo was also part of the Ratu Kadavulevu School team that won the Super Deans title in 2015.
